items.title: AI-designed protein tricks defective insulin receptors into working in new mouse study
items.excerpt: Scientists report that a de novo protein designed with AI can activate broken insulin receptors in mice, pointing to a possible route for treating severe insulin resistance. The designed 'key' binds a receptor whose natural lock is defective.

items.title: Watch out, AlphaFold: Claude and ChatGPT's new biology skills wow scientists
items.excerpt: Anthropic's and OpenAI's general-purpose language models can now design proteins and predict their sequences and structures — capabilities previously seen only in specialized tools such as AlphaFold. Researchers report lab binding data for model-designed candidates.

items.title: De novo design of high-potency dual-target therapeutic peptides with ORIDTP
items.excerpt: The ORIDTP platform designs dual-target therapeutic peptides from scratch, producing candidates with strong in vivo efficacy across anti-obesity, antidiabetic and anticancer targets. The authors report broad cross-target generalizability.

items.title: AI-assisted method advances high-resolution structure classification of membrane proteins in vesicles
items.excerpt: Chinese Academy of Sciences researchers trained a model to estimate vesicle membrane geometry and use it to filter cryo-EM particles, reaching 2.7 A for influenza hemagglutinin in vesicles. The isSPA-vesicle approach extends to proteins too small for the original framework (PNAS).

items.title: AI helps chemists design the next generation of artificial enzymes
items.excerpt: Birmingham, Edinburgh and Oxford chemists made and tested 30 palladium molecular cages that mimic enzymes, then used machine learning on the rate data to link shape, volume and electrostatics to catalytic activity (JACS). The model turns cage catalysis into a data-driven design problem.

items.title: Scientists Use AI-Designed CRISPR to Make Disease-Resistant Rice
items.excerpt: University of Missouri researchers adapted Profluent's AI-designed gene editor OpenCRISPR-1 for rice, hitting up to 97% editing success in a research variety. Edited plants resisted three strains of the bacterial blight pathogen and passed the edits to offspring.

items.title: Stabilizing atomically thin metals with sandwich structures: Machine learning expands the search
items.excerpt: University of Jyvaskyla researchers trained machine-learning models on first-principles data to screen over a thousand metallene 'sandwich' heterostructures, finding more than 300 stable candidates (Nano Letters). Selected structures stayed intact and metallic in room-temperature simulations.

items.title: One random shot or none: A mathematical proof for learning a physical system from one experiment
items.excerpt: Cornell researchers proved a zero-one law: if any single experiment can reveal a system's governing equations for a broad class of models, then almost any random experiment can too (PNAS). The result bounds when machine-learned physical models are identifiable.

items.title: Suppressing starlight reveals new exoplanets
items.excerpt: Physics-based image-processing algorithms strip residual starlight from direct-imaging data, letting astronomers pick out planets previously too faint to see. The team reports new detections from reprocessed observations.

items.title: Machine learning reveals new Galactic C-rich and O-rich AGB sources
items.excerpt: A classifier trained on known asymptotic-giant-branch stars identifies new carbon-rich and oxygen-rich AGB sources across Galactic survey photometry. Accepted for publication in MNRAS.

items.title: Unsupervised Machine Learning Classification of FRB 20121102A across Distinct Active Episodes
items.excerpt: Unsupervised clustering of bursts from the repeating fast radio burst FRB 20121102A separates distinct active episodes, implying changes in the source's emission state. Accepted for publication.

items.title: Learning to find cosmic filaments with graph neural networks
items.excerpt: A graph neural network traces the cosmic web's filamentary structure directly from galaxy catalogues, outperforming classical filament finders. Accepted at the Machine Learning and the Physical Sciences workshop.

items.title: The Physics Wall Facing Orbital AI Data Centers
items.excerpt: A new preprint by NASA JPL's Slava Turyshev works through the thermodynamics and radiator mass budgets of orbiting AI data centres and finds the business plans run into hard physics limits. The analysis puts numbers on heat rejection, power and launch mass.

items.title: From spectrum to structure: Identifying molecules with Mass Spec Skills for Google Antigravity
items.excerpt: DeepMind released Mass Spec Skills, letting Gemini agents interpret tandem mass spectra by driving established tools and public chemical databases. On a 100-compound benchmark exact-match identification rose to about 97%, from under 4% without the skills.

items.title: Finding faster quantum algorithms with agents and formal verification
items.excerpt: Teams of Gemini agents improved known quantum algorithms with every result Lean-verified, including an 11.8x cheaper fusion-related calculation, 8x cheaper photochemistry simulation and 2.5x for cytochrome P450. The work is posted as arXiv:2611.09822.

items.title: Verifiable Social Reasoning for LLM Assistants
items.excerpt: Google Research built a multi-agent simulation that tests whether assistants can infer a third party's hidden motive from a user's one-sided account, and released over 20,000 generated cases. Twelve LLMs were evaluated against the ground-truth motives (arXiv:2609.17496).

items.title: Empirical evidence for eight ways that AI is impacting people
items.excerpt: A review weighs the actual evidence behind eight widely repeated concerns about AI's effect on people, finding only modest support for the most alarming claims. The authors call for sharper empirical scrutiny of human impact.

items.title: What is a thought made of? Why human consciousness may be beyond AI's reach
items.excerpt: A new theory argues the brain chemically encodes and retrieves memories rather than relying on electrical signalling alone, with molecular surroundings tying memory to emotion. The authors argue this chemistry is why current AI architectures may not reproduce consciousness.

items.title: A legendary philosopher isn't buying Anthropic's consciousness argument
items.excerpt: Anthropic told investors its models might be conscious while warning that acting on it could hurt the business. A veteran philosopher of mind picks apart the argument and what an AI-welfare policy would actually require.

items.title: Scientists at Meta decode typed sentences from brain activity without surgically implanted chips
items.excerpt: A Nature Neuroscience study from Meta shows magnetoencephalography plus a trained model can reconstruct typed sentences from outside the skull, without implants. Accuracy trails invasive interfaces but needs no surgery.

items.title: Machine-learning models can detect elevated psychopathy and sadism from reactions to funny pictures
items.excerpt: Algorithms trained on how people rate cartoons and memes picked out elevated psychopathy, sadism and narcissism from humour preferences alone. Machiavellianism left no detectable trace.

items.title: This AI Tweaks LLM Neural Networks Like a Gene Editor
items.excerpt: Researchers describe a system that edits specific circuits inside a language model the way a gene editor rewrites DNA, changing behaviour without retraining. The approach borrows directly from molecular-biology methodology.
